proofs.full_local_argument: Curator reconstruction of the short source argument, explicitly separated from source text; not a new Theorem or an author-issued correction. Put b=rho_bar, h=phi_{1/b}, p=p_t and g=G(x_t,xi_t). Since p is feasible and proj_X(p)=p, h(x_{t+1})<=f(p)+(b/2)||p-x_{t+1}||^2<=f(p)+(b/2)||p-x_t+alpha_t*g||^2. Taking E_t and using E_t g=v_t and E_t||g||^2<=L^2 gives E_t h(x_{t+1})<=h(x_t)+b*alpha_t*<p-x_t,v_t>+(b/2)*alpha_t^2*L^2. Weak convexity gives <p-x_t,v_t><=f(p)-f(x_t)+(rho/2)||p-x_t||^2. Define q_t(y)=f(y)+(b/2)||y-x_t||^2+iota_X(y). It is (b-rho)-strongly convex and p minimizes it, so q_t(x_t)-q_t(p)>=(b-rho)||x_t-p||^2/2. Expanding q_t and adding (b-rho)||x_t-p||^2/2 shows f(x_t)-f(p)-(rho/2)||x_t-p||^2 >= (b-rho)||x_t-p||^2. Therefore E_t h(x_{t+1})<=h(x_t)-b*alpha_t*(b-rho)||x_t-p||^2+(b/2)*alpha_t^2*L^2 = h(x_t)-alpha_t*(b-rho)/b*||gradient h(x_t)||^2+(b/2)*alpha_t^2*L^2. Total expectation proves Eq.(3.3). Summing gives ((b-rho)/b)*sum alpha_t E||gradient h(x_t)||^2 <= h(x0)-E h(x_{T+1})+(b*L^2/2)*Q <= Delta_b+(b*L^2/2)*Q. The conditional output distribution implies E||gradient h(x_R)||^2=(sum alpha_t E||gradient h(x_t)||^2)/S. Division proves Eq.(3.4), with no additional b in the denominator. For b=2rho and alpha_t=gamma/sqrt(T+1), Q=gamma^2, S=gamma*sqrt(T+1), and b/(b-rho)=2, proving Eq.(3.5). All finite-horizon expectations used here are well-defined: the second-moment Oracle bound and projection nonexpansiveness imply finite second moments of x_t-x0 by induction. Because f+(rho/2)||.||^2 is finite convex on R^d, a subgradient at x0 supplies a quadratic lower bound for f. With phi bounded below by phi_star, a proximal minimizer exists uniquely; comparison with the feasible x0 bounds ||p_t-x0|| by an affine function of ||x_t-x0|| using strong convexity and a subgradient at x0. Thus p_t and gradient h(x_t)=b(x_t-p_t) have finite second moments. Also phi_star<=h(x_t)<=f(x0)+(b/2)||x_t-x0||^2, so the envelope expectations are finite.
proofs.locator: p.13 Eq.(3.6)–(3.8), strong-convexity comparison; p.14 conditional descent, telescoping and output averaging
map: Let F_t contain xi_0,...,xi_{t-1}, v_t=E[G(x_t,xi_t)|F_t], and p_t=prox_{phi/rho_bar}(x_t). Both x_t and p_t are F_t-measurable, p_t is feasible, and v_t belongs to partial f(x_t).

Eq.(3.6) tests the envelope minimization at p_t. Nonexpansiveness of projection, expansion of the squared norm, and A(A3) give E_t phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_{t+1}) <= phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_t)+rho_bar*alpha_t*<p_t-x_t,v_t>+(rho_bar*alpha_t^2*L^2)/2.
Eq.(2.5) bounds <p_t-x_t,v_t> by f(p_t)-f(x_t)+(rho/2)||p_t-x_t||^2, yielding Eq.(3.8).

Strong convexity of f(y)+(rho_bar/2)||y-x_t||^2 on X, with modulus rho_bar-rho, gives f(x_t)-f(p_t)-(rho/2)||x_t-p_t||^2 >= (rho_bar-rho)||x_t-p_t||^2. Lemma 2.2 converts squared distance to envelope gradient squared divided by rho_bar^2.

Substitution yields conditional descent; total expectation gives Eq.(3.3). Sum over t=0,...,T and lower-bound the final envelope by phi_star. Divide by S and use the output distribution for Eq.(3.4). Substitute rho_bar=2rho and the constant steps for Eq.(3.5). The extra denominator rho_bar in the intermediate p.14 weighted-average display is not used.

assumptions: f:R^d->R is rho-weakly convex: f+(rho/2)||.||^2 is convex; rho>=0. X is nonempty closed convex, and the finite attained minimum condition above makes the source notation min phi explicit. No bounded diameter or smoothness assumption is imposed.
Assumption A(A1): On a probability space (Omega,F,P), iid realizations xi_t are available, independent of past samples.
Assumption A(A2): There is an open U containing X and a measurable mapping G:U x Omega->R^d with E_xi G(x,xi) in partial f(x) for every x in U, using the subdifferential defined in §2.2.
Assumption A(A3): For some finite L>=0 and every x in X, E_xi||G(x,xi)||^2<=L^2. This bounds the full second moment, not merely the variance.
Initialize a deterministic x0 in X. For t=0,...,T, use fresh xi_t and exact update x_{t+1}=proj_X(x_t-alpha_t G(x_t,xi_t)), with deterministic alpha_t>0.
Draw R in {0,...,T} with conditional probability alpha_t/S given the trajectory, using additional randomization, and return x_R.
statement.conclusion: Eq.(3.3): E[phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_{t+1})] <= E[phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_t)] - alpha_t*(rho_bar-rho)/rho_bar * E||gradient phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_t)||^2 + alpha_t^2*rho_bar*L^2/2. Eq.(3.4): E||gradient phi_{1/rho_bar}(x_R)||^2 <= [rho_bar/(rho_bar-rho)]*[Delta_{rho_bar}+(rho_bar*L^2/2)*Q]/S. Eq.(3.5): if rho>0, rho_bar=2rho and alpha_t=gamma/sqrt(T+1), then E||gradient phi_{1/(2rho)}(x_R)||^2 <= 2*[phi_{1/(2rho)}(x0)-phi_star+rho*L^2*gamma^2]/[gamma*sqrt(T+1)].
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^d with d a positive integer. X is nonempty closed convex, iota_X is 0 on X and +infinity otherwise, phi=f+iota_X, and phi_star=min_{x in X} f(x) is finite and attained in this recorded scope. For lambda>0, phi_lambda(x)=min_{y in X}{f(y)+||y-x||^2/(2lambda)}. For rho_bar>rho, its unique proximal point is p(x)=argmin_{y in X}{f(y)+(rho_bar/2)||y-x||^2} and gradient phi_{1/rho_bar}(x)=rho_bar*(x-p(x)). Let Delta_{rho_bar}=phi_{1/rho_bar}(x0)-phi_star, S=sum_{t=0}^T alpha_t and Q=sum_{t=0}^T alpha_t^2.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1 integer; T>=0 integer; rho>=0; finite L>=0; rho_bar>rho; alpha_t>0 with no upper bound. The Eq.(3.5) specialization additionally requires rho>0, rho_bar=2rho and any gamma>0 with alpha_t=gamma/sqrt(T+1).
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every instance satisfying these conditions, every x0 in X, finite integer T>=0, deterministic positive steps alpha_0,...,alpha_T, and rho_bar>rho, the conclusions hold. Expectations include the iid Oracle samples and, for x_R, the additional output draw. The one-step conclusion holds for each t=0,...,T.
